question: Will the fastest official time at the 2026 World Bog Snorkelling Championships be under 1:15.00?

factors.description: Sub-1:15 achieved only once in event history (Rutter 2023 WR 1:12.35), an outlier even for the only capable athlete
Rutter typically wins in ~1:18 range (1:18.81 in 2018, 1:18.13 in 2025), comfortably above the threshold
Rutter's 2026 participation unconfirmed; when he was absent (2024) fastest was ~1:29, far above threshold
Rutter is an active, motivated record-chaser who did break 1:15 once, so a repeat is plausible if conditions favor it

summary: Sub-1:15 is essentially a Neil-Rutter-only phenomenon — his 2023 record (1:12.35) is the only sub-1:15 time ever recorded at these championships. YES requires both that Rutter competes in 2026 (~70%, given his 2025 return but unconfirmed status) AND that he swims a near-record time (~25-30%, since even he usually finishes ~1:18, breaking 1:15 in only 1 of ~3 recent appearances). The non-Rutter field consistently runs 1:22+. Conditional decomposition yields ~0.70×0.27 + 0.30×0.02 ≈ 0.19, discounted slightly to ~0.15 for status-quo stickiness and Rutter's typical above-threshold finishes.

The question asks whether the fastest official time at the 2026 World Bog Snorkelling Championships will be under 1:15.00. Key reasoning:

- **Sub-1:15 is a once-in-history event** — only Neil Rutter's 2023 world record (1:12.35) has ever broken 1:15 in this competition.
- **Even Rutter usually finishes ~1:18** (1:18.81 in 2018, 1:18.13 in 2025), comfortably above the threshold.
- **The non-Rutter field runs 1:22+** — when Rutter was absent in 2024, the fastest time was ~1:29.
- **Rutter's 2026 participation is unconfirmed** (retired after 2023, returned in 2025).

YES requires the conjunction of Rutter competing (~70%) and him producing a near-record swim (~25-30%), giving roughly 0.19, which I discount slightly to **0.15** for status-quo stickiness.
